notes: Dept of Commerce (CHIPS R&D Office) finalized a CHIPS Act award of up to $100M to D-Wave Quantum Inc. (NASDAQ: QBTS) to advance semiconductor process tech for annealing and gate-model superconducting quantum systems (target: 100,000-qubit annealing system; 10,000-qubit gate-model system). Mandatory condition: Commerce receives a minority, non-controlling equity stake in D-Wave via share issuance -- same CHIPS equity-kicker structure as Rigetti/Intel (Rigetti already on file, not duplicated here). Part of a ~$2.0B package across 9 quantum companies (GlobalFoundries $375M and Rigetti $100M already on file from last run; Quantinuum, PsiQuantum, Anderon filed this run; Infleqtion/Diraq LOIs not yet finalized, not filed). Source is D-Wave's own press release, furnished as Exhibit 99.1 to its 8-K (SEC EDGAR, resolved filing). Corroborated by NIST (nist.gov/news-events/news/2026/09/department-commerce-announces-finalization-chips-rd-award-d-wave, same date) and trade press (Quantum Computing Report, HPCwire).

Dept of Commerce finalized a CHIPS Act R&D award of up to $100M to Quantinuum (Honeywell-majority-owned, mid-IPO-process per its FY2026 S-1/A on file with SEC) for trapped-ion quantum computer manufacturing -- low-loss integrated photonics, cryogenic-use semiconductors, optical components at trapped-ion wavelengths -- adding onshore supply partners GlobalFoundries and Monarch Quantum. Only trapped-ion architecture in the 9-company, ~$2.0B CHIPS quantum package. Confirmed by Quantinuum's own IR release (ir.quantinuum.com, same date, 2026-09-08 07:30) and wide trade pickup (HPCwire, Quantum Computing Report, Yahoo Finance/PR Newswire).

Dept of Commerce finalized a CHIPS Act R&D award of up to $100M to PsiQuantum, converting its May-2026 $100M Letter of Intent into a definitive agreement. Funds 300mm wafer production of barium titanate (electro-optic thin-film material) via MBE at PsiQuantum's Santa Clara, CA facility, plus high-temp single-photon detectors and ultra-low-loss photonic packaging. Commerce takes a minority, non-controlling equity stake as a condition of the award (same structure across the 9-company CHIPS quantum package). Confirmed by PsiQuantum's own release (psiquantum.com/news-import) and trade press (Quantum Computing Report, HPCwire, The Quantum Insider), all dated 2026-09-08.

Dept of Commerce finalized a CHIPS Act R&D award of up to $1B to Anderon, a newly formed IBM subsidiary, to accelerate its 300mm quantum wafer foundry in Albany, NY (superconducting qubit arrays, quantum I/O signaling, readout signal chain -- production already underway). IBM itself is matching with an equal ~$1B of its own capital (IBM's own money is not this allocator's row -- only the US Government's $1B award is recorded here). By far the largest of the 9 CHIPS quantum-package awards (GlobalFoundries $375M, five others $100M each, ~$2.0B total). Confirmed by IBM's own newsroom release (newsroom.ibm.com, same date, also carried on PR Newswire) and trade press (The Quantum Insider, Quantum Zeitgeist, DigiTimes).
